title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting: G is a stable 'graph type' (dual graph of a stable marked curve), and M_G is the moduli space (or stack) of curves of exact type G. G' is a less degenerate type obtained by smoothing (plumbing) some of the nodes of G. SP_G is the principal bundle over M_G of rigidifications by unit tangent directions at the nodes and marked points. Its structure group is a torus U^{Â}, and on the previous page this bundle is split as P_C ×_{M_G} P_B. The page sets ST_G := π_1(SP_G), a 'Teichmüller group' attached to the stratum G. This group is a central extension of the orbifold π_1(M_G) by Z^{Â}; the kernel is generated by loops of tangent directions, i.e. Dehn twists around the vanishing cycles. On the previous page Grothendieck replaced M_G by a homotopy-equivalent space M̃^C_G: curves of type G together with chosen disks D_i (local coordinates) around the branches of the nodes in C. Over M̃^C_G he took P̃^B_G, the pullback of the U^B-torsor P_B, so that ST_G ≃ π_1(P̃^B_G). This page then gives three steps. (1) There is a cartesian square P̃^B_G → SP_{G'} over M̃^C_G → M_{G'}. The bottom arrow is plumbing: from (X,(D_i)) and a choice of gluing angles, build a smooth-at-those-nodes curve X' of type G'. Cartesianness says that the U^B-torsor of unit tangent directions of X' at its remaining special points is canonically (even 'equal') the one P_{B,X} coming from X. (2) Taking π_1 gives a homomorphism ST_G → ST_{G'}. This is the 'clutching' or 'boundary specialization' map from the Teichmüller group of a boundary stratum to that of a less degenerate one; in modern terms it is π_1 of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of the stratum mapping into the open stratum, with the U^1 tangent data playing the role of tangential base points. (3) To build that neighbourhood, he lets the multiplicative topological monoid ]0,1] (unit 1) act, in its power over C, on M̃^C_G by homotheties of the disks D_i (shrinking the plumbing collars). In a marginal correction he takes one parameter per edge (ρ of the two orientations of α equal) instead of one per oriented branch, 'otherwise there are dummy parameters'. This reflects that plumbing zw = t depends only on the product of the two radii. The next page combines this action with the U^B-torsor to get a map M_C × M̃^C_G → M_{G'}. That map plays the role of the inclusion of the punctured tubular neighbourhood V*_{G,G'} of M_G in the compactification, and it is used to define the Teichmüller-group maps between strata, which are the 'Lego' gluing data of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible. The morphism π_1(P̃^B_G) → π_1(SP_{G'}) is only defined up to base points / inner automorphisms; it should be read as a map of fundamental groupoids, consistent with the cartesian square.

The marginal remark correctly fixes an over-parametrisation: separate homothety ratios on the two disks at a node give the same plumbed curve up to isomorphism, since only the product matters. So with one ratio per oriented branch the monoid would not act freely and effectively on the relevant parameter space. Since ]0,1] is contractible, this does not affect π_1 statements, only the honesty of the 'tubular neighbourhood' model.

ideas.what: Teichmüller group of a boundary stratum defined as π_1 of the bundle of unit-tangent rigidifications at the nodes (central extension by the Dehn-twist lattice Z^{edges})
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the stratum with tangential base points / stabilizer of a multicurve in the mapping class group; Lego/Teichmüller tower building blocks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984), worked out by Ihara–Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §§2-3 (Teichmüller tower, base points 'at infinity'), only sketchily

ideas.what: Plumbing map M̃^C_G (curves with chosen disks at nodes) → M_{G'} and the cartesian square identifying the unit-tangent torsors of X and X'
ideas.modern_name: plumbing coordinates / clutching construction near the Deligne–Mumford boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bers, Earle–Marden, Kra, Wolpert; Deligne–Mumford/Knudsen for the algebraic boundary

ideas.what: Induced homomorphism ST_G → ST_{G'}, i.e. the map from the stratum's Teichmüller group into that of a less degenerate stratum
ideas.modern_name: inclusion of a multicurve stabilizer / π_1 of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum (Ihara–Nakamura 'Teichmüller–Lego' maps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to it

ideas.what: Action of the topological monoid ]0,1]^C (one parameter per edge) by homotheties of the plumbing disks, modelling the radial direction of the punctured tubular neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: radial plumbing parameter / real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama log-geometric boundary) of the Deligne–Mumford boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kato–Nakayama (1999) for log Betti realization; Looijenga; Harvey/Ivanov for bordification

missed.claim: Grothendieck models the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a stratum as a product of a contractible monoid ]0,1]^C with a U^B-torsor of unit tangent directions over a stratum enriched by disk coordinates. This is essentially the real oriented blow-up / Kato–Nakayama space of the log structure on the boundary, written down in a topos-theoretic setting around 1978–84. It anticipates the log-Betti description later used in Teichmüller tower work (e.g. Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki), but the idea itself is known and was rediscovered.
missed.quote: Considérons le monoïde topologique multiplicatif ]0,1] (avec élément unité 1) et sa puissance C-ième ... il vaut mieux prendre ]0,1]^C, sinon il y a des "paramètres bidon"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck had a concrete homotopy model for the boundary maps of the Teichmüller tower, which the Esquisse leaves vague.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard construction (plumbing, tangential base points, boundary maps between Teichmüller groups). It anticipates later Ihara–Nakamura / log-geometric treatments, but these are well established and the Esquisse already indicates the idea.
transcription_corrections: 'la M_C-fibre M̃^C_C' should read 'la M_G-fibré M̃^C_G' (the M_G-bundle M̃^C_G).
'M_{\vec C} = ]0,1]^{\vec C}' is written with a script/blackboard M, matching the 'm_C' that 'opère' (the monoid is denoted 𝕄_C or 𝓜_C, as on the next page).
Margin note: 'on prend ρ_{\vec α} = ρ_{\overleftarrow α} pour \vec α, \overleftarrow α sur α ∈ C', i.e. equal ratios on the two branches of each edge.
Label on the vertical arrow: 'U^B-tors. sur M̃^C_G'.
